readmeHtml:
Custom CSS reset

Browsers ship with default styles. Those defaults can create or seem like inconsistencies when building across different browsers—for example, differences in line-height can affect spacing, height, and alignment.

While browser standards have improved over time and inconsistencies have reduced, defaults still vary enough that a reset stylesheet remains a useful starting point.

One of the earliest widely used reset stylesheets was Eric Meyer's (2011). Eric recommended tailoring resets to suit your needs. A lot has changed since then, so this project provides an updated, generic reset you can adapt.

This reset stylesheet is a collection based on real usage from work done and inspection of modern, well-built sites. It’s intended to be a strong baseline that you can modify to suit your needs.

Getting Started

You could introuduce this into your project by either;

  1. Copy the reset.css file into your project or
  2. Import it at the top of your main stylesheet so it loads before your app styles.
 @import "./reset.css";

Note

  • Apply the reset as the starting base of a project - best applied that way.
  • Avoid introducing it into an existing codebase unless you are prepared to address layout/style changes.
readmeExcerpt:
# Custom CSS reset

Browsers ship with default styles. Those defaults can create or seem like inconsistencies when building across different browsers—for example, differences in line-height can affect spacing, height, and alignment.

While browser standards have improved over time and inconsistencies have reduced, defaults still vary enough that a reset stylesheet remains a useful starting point.

One of the earliest widely used reset stylesheets was [Eric Meyer's](https://meyerweb.com/eric/tools/css/reset/) (2011). Eric recommended tailoring resets to suit your needs. A lot has changed since then, so this project provides an updated, generic reset you can adapt.

This reset stylesheet is a collection based on real usage from work done and inspection of modern, well-built sites. It’s intended to be a strong baseline that you can modify to suit your needs.

---

## Getting Started
You could introuduce this into your project by either;
1. Copy the reset.css file into your project or 
2. Import it at the top of your main stylesheet so it loads before your app styles.

```css
 @import "./reset.css";
```

---

### Note

* Apply the reset as the starting base of a project - best applied that way.
* Avoid introducing it into an existing codebase unless you are prepared to address layout/style changes.

---

aiSummary.oneLiner: Custom CSS reset stylesheet tailored for modern browsers and web standards.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project provides a modern, custom CSS reset stylesheet designed to neutralize browser-specific default styles. It builds upon classic approaches like Eric Meyer's reset but updates them for current web development practices based on real-world usage and inspection of well-built sites. By eliminating inconsistencies in line-heights, spacing, and alignment across different browsers, it provides a strong, predictable baseline for developers to build upon and customize. It specifically targets modern HTML elements and layout edge-cases to provide a solid foundational starting point for contemporary CSS architectures.
keyFeatures: Modern Baseline: Updated to reflect current browser standards and layout practices.
Cross-Browser Consistency: Eliminates default styling variations across different rendering engines.
Customizable Foundation: Designed as a generic starting point intended for developers to modify for their specific needs.
Easy Integration: Can be imported directly or copied into projects as the very first stylesheet.
Real-World Tested: Based on actual usage and inspection of modern production websites.
Modern styling baseline: Updates traditional reset techniques to accommodate the behavior of modern browsers and HTML5 elements.
